verdict.rationale: Alacritty's own config lets users cap or disable the scrollback buffer, which limits how much terminal output it keeps. That is a thin, local form of retention control. Nothing documents deletion or clearing of history, or any broader data-retention posture. Missing for 10: documented history clearing/deletion controls, an explicit statement on persistence (e.g. no on-disk logging), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: Maximum number of lines in the scrollback buffer. Specifying 0 will disable scrolling. Limited to 100000.
